svg.title: Wall shoot and park: C1, shoot 4 (tips the HIVE), left corridor to the LOADING ZONE - BLUE alliance
svg.desc: Top view of the 141.35 by 141.35 inch BIOBUZZ field, audience at the bottom, red alliance on the left. Route wall_shoot_park for the BLUE alliance, starting in tile C1, with 6 steps: 1 START at (83.3, 131.6, 90 deg); 2 SHOOT 4 at UP cell from the solver's pose; 3 DRIVE along the wall constant to 111.3, 126.5; 4 DRIVE corridor reverse tangent to 111.3, 41.3; 5 DRIVE to zone linear to 129.3, 33.3; 6 PARK at (129.3, 33.3, 180 deg). First tip: we shoot the first tip. Estimated 12.4 s, POLLEN balance -4, up to 28 points for our robot; 0 errors and 1 warnings.

id wall_shoot_park | start tile C1 | 6 steps | blue ink | first tip: we shoot the first tip

g.title: step 2: move to the pose of SHOOT

step 3: DRIVE along the wall constant to 111.3, 126.5 (t = 6.2 to 7.9 s) - Slides sideways along the audience wall, STAYING LOW and keeping the front toward the wall (at the nominal shooting pose the center is only 12.1 in from the wall and a robot that turns on the spot there swings a corner 1.1 in through it). Staying low matters for the tip: what falls out of the tipped cell lands up to 40 in out from the HIVE's middle line, and the robot's rear edge (14.8 + 8.03 = 22.8 in from the wall) is 47.8 in out, so it is clear of the spill (G409) until it is beside the cell, where it turns up the corridor.

step 4: DRIVE corridor reverse tangent to 111.3, 41.3 (t = 7.9 to 11.0 s) - Straight up the left corridor, backwards (the shooter end first), 12.9 in (center to keep-out) clear of the HIVE frame keep-out at x 42.94 and clear of the spill zone (x 41.39 and more) beside it.
step 5: DRIVE to zone linear to 129.3, 33.3 (t = 11.0 to 12.4 s) - Turns to face +x while sliding into the zone.

step 1: START at (83.3, 131.6, 90 deg) (t = 0.0 to 0.0 s) - Front edge ON the audience wall (the center of rotation is 9.77 in out). Place the robot with the wheel tips touching the wall and the middle of the robot over tile C1.

step 2: SHOOT 4 at UP cell from the solver's pose (t = 0.0 to 6.2 s) - AUTO pose: the solver stands about 34 in in front of the cell; the diagram shows the nominal pose. The 3 staged NECTAR plus the 3rd POLLEN tip the HIVE: one volley is the first tip, and the 4th pre-load is the spare for a stiff HIVE (the camera cannot stop the feeder before the 4th is launched, so it is probably spent). - pose drawn is the nominal standoff pose; the solver picks the real one

g.title: WARN step 2 [G417] step 2 (SHOOT, the move to its pose): the HIVE tips with POLLEN 3 of the 4 (3 NECTAR in the cell; a cell tips at 8 POLLEN-equivalents (each POLLEN counts 1, each NECTAR 5/3)), but the camera cannot stop the feeder at once: the POLLEN that tips it is in the air for 0.50 s and the feeder stops about 0.85 s after it lands (Auto.TIP_STOP_LATENCY_SEC), while the next POLLEN leaves 0.90 s after the last. So the next 1 POLLEN will probably be launched into the cell while it swings down (G417: a launch at a rocking HIVE can spoil the tip; QA12 lets you add elements to a HIVE that is moving) and is spent: the plan counts 4 fired and 0 of the spare kept. The spare is for a field that needs one more POLLEN, not a POLLEN to carry on. Fire only 3 to keep it for sure (no spare then), or measure the real stop time on day one: with a latency under 0.40 s the spare stays in the robot
